title: 2026-10-22_XOR.DDoS_Incident_Response_a56
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating and responding to an XOR.DDoS malware infection on a Linux-based host. The malware is designed to force infected hosts to participate in large DDoS attack campaigns. Your goal is to identify the malicious activity, contain the threat, and remove the malware from the infected host.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating and responding to an XOR.DDoS malware infection on a Linux-based host. The malware is designed to force infected hosts to participate in large DDoS attack campaigns. Your goal is to identify the malicious activity, contain the threat, and remove the malware from the infected host.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: To access the sandbox in the cloud, use the following credentials: username: trainee, password: trainee123. Enter 'start' to begin the training.
levels.local_content: To access the local sandbox, use the following credentials: username: trainee, password: trainee123. Enter 'start' to begin the training.

levels.title: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the host
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Your task is to identify and investigate any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the host that could be responsible for this activity.
levels.solution: Check the list of running services and look for any that are not part of the standard system configuration. The hidden flag is the name of the suspicious service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Consider the methods used to identify unauthorized or suspicious services on a system.

hints.title: Actionable Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all running services.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system configuration or have unusual names.

levels.title: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot
levels.content: You have identified a suspicious service running on the host. Your next task is to determine how this service is automatically started after a system reboot.
levels.solution: Check the systemd service files and timers to see if the suspicious service is configured to start automatically. The hidden flag is the name of the systemd service or persistence identifier.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Think about the mechanisms that can be used to automatically start services after a system reboot.

hints.title: Actionable Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-unit-files --type=service' to list all service unit files.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: Look for service unit files that are enabled and have unusual names or paths.

levels.title: Locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious activity
levels.content: You have identified the suspicious service and its persistence mechanism. Your next task is to locate the executable or file associated with this suspicious activity.
levels.solution: Check the process information and look for the executable path associated with the suspicious service. The hidden flag is the filename or file path of the malicious executable.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Consider the methods used to locate executables or files associated with suspicious activity on a system.

hints.title: Actionable Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'ps aux' to list all running processes and their associated executables.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: Look for processes that have unusual executable paths or names.
